text:
alex: Heads up — deploy-bot is about to tag a minor bump for the checkout fix in #PR-3421. It detected a change but misclassified it as a feature. I'm leaning patch (2.4.2). Thoughts?

release-bot: deploy plan check: detected files: src/checkout/*.rs, tests/checkout/* -> heuristics: non-doc + src change => candidate minor. Tagging rules: if PR title matches /BREAKING|FEATURE/ => minor, else patch.

maria: This is definitely a bugfix, non-breaking. We should avoid minor bumps during the stable release window unless it's a new capability. Patch + changelog entry.

jamal: Agree with maria. Also: if deploy-bot is ambiguous, we should prefer patch and add a manual override flag. Otherwise downstream consumers see unnecessary semver noise.

paul: +1 patch. Quick ops note: release-bot respects [PATCH] or [MINOR] tokens in the PR title. If you retitle with [PATCH] it'll force the right tag. Also we can run `./scripts/releasebot --force-patch` for a manual override.

alex: Ok I'll retitle to "[PATCH] checkout: avoid null ptr on empty cart" and add a changelog snippet.

release-bot: automatic tag applied: v2.4.2 by @alex (CI job #4821).

maria: Nice. Can we add a brief note to the release-channel so product knows it's not a feature? :eyes:

alex: Posting now: "v2.4.2 (patch) — bugfix for checkout NPE, no behavioral changes, safe to roll forward" :tada:

jamal: small follow-up: can we file a tiny RFC to tighten heuristics? Example: if change only touches error handling or test files, prefer patch. Saves us surprises.

paul: SGTM. Also pro-tip: for buildmeta-heavy runs, use `--no-buildmeta` to avoid CI build hashes ending up in tag names for patches.

alex: Filed RFC draft in #releng (link: https://git.internal/rex/rfcs/semver-heuristics) and updated PR. Thanks all, closing thread.
